reconcile.note: Fausset and his co-authors read 1 Thessalonians' imminence and 2 Thessalonians' apostasy-first requirement as successive stages of one unfolding revelation.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg reads Second Thessalonians as a later writer branding First Thessalonians a forgery, exposing incompatible timelines under Paul's name.

quotes.text: The author of Second Thessalonians, whose epistle is a self-evident forgery, declares First Thessalonians to be a forgery.
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), ch. "The Epistles of Paul," on 1 Thessalonians 4:15 and 2 Thessalonians 2:2.

sides.snippet: we who are alive, who are left to the coming of the Lord, will in no way precede those who have fallen asleep
sides.verseText: For this we tell you by the word of the Lord, that we who are alive, who are left to the coming of the Lord, will in no way precede those who have fallen asleep.

sides.snippet: not to be quickly shaken in your mind, nor yet be troubled
sides.verseText: not to be quickly shaken in your mind, nor yet be troubled, either by spirit, or by word, or by letter as from us, saying that the day of Christ had come.
